input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together in a playground. Each of you has a toy car, and you all want to race and play together at the same time. Now, if you all just drive around without talking, you might crash into each other or not know where everyone is.

But what if you all have walkie-talkies? You can talk to each other very quickly and tell each other where you are and what you’re doing. A computer game like CoD or WoW is a bit like that playground, but instead of walkie-talkies, the computers use something called the “internet” to talk to each other super fast.

The game has a special helper called a “server.” The server is like a big brain that listens to everyone playing and tells everyone else where each player is, what they’re doing, and what’s happening in the game. This happens so quickly that it feels like you’re all playing together at the same time, even if your friends are far away!

So, the game uses the internet and special computers to make sure everyone’s toy car (or character) moves the right way, so it looks like you’re all playing together in the same world.
